jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 258158

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Director, International Wealth Management is accountable for developing, leading, and overseeing delivery teams who are responsible for working with cross-functional development teams and business stakeholders to define and implement business strategies, product roadmaps, service offerings and new features.

The Director contributes to the long-term profitability of the International Wealth Management business line by establishing performance goals and work practices which drive the design and development of high-quality products and solutions.

This is a demanding hands-on and strategic role which requires the incumbent to be knowledgeable of the financial services sector and emerging trends in the Wealth and Asset Management industry.

Is this role right for you? In this role you will:

Management and oversight for delivery of a portfolio of initiatives focused on client and advisor solutions, ensuring that the deliverable align with strategic priorities.
Lead and drive a customer focused culture throughout the delivery teams to influence a client-centered design culture and to deepen relationships with business stakeholders and leverage broader bank relationships, systems, processes and knowledge.
Understand and keep up to date with emerging technologies, trends and innovative solutions across the industry.
Collaborate with business SMEs and technology teams to create platform roadmaps that align and assist in moving business strategies forward.
Provide guidance to stakeholders to ensure prioritization is driven by business value.
Define, lead and execute a cohesive strategy designed to limit technological debt and to effectively manage transition from legacy systems to modern technology platforms, maximizing operational efficiencies.
Excellent relationship building, influencing and negotiation skills to build and maintain strong supportive relationships with stakeholders across the organization.
Manage engagement with bank stakeholders and effectively communicate product release contents and expected product capabilities/customer journey.
Engage with the engineering and design teams to help determine the best technical implementation methods as well as a reasonable implementation schedule to launch products on a regular basis.
Manage communications and status reporting of ongoing initiatives, including summarizing project risks and options and facilitating prompt decisions when needed.
Maintain an understanding of financial services markets, the competitive landscape and digital transformation trends relative to the Wealth and Asset Management sector and client/user needs and requirements.
You possess a visionary and strategic leadership while inspiring team of solution architects and engineers to embrace your vision and be best in class team responsible for implementing and maintaining Wealth Technology solutions.
You are future focused with the ability to develop roadmaps and build business cases including benefits and costs
You thrive in providing strong leadership and driving employee empowerment and a high degree of engagement.
You excel in overseeing the architecture and design of solutions for the enterprise in a large and distributed environment.
You have experience delivering complex projects providing global, innovative solutions that improve the delivery of Wealth products
You excel in the assessment and selection of Global Wealth technologies and integration partners.
You excel in relationship, stakeholder management and influencing and negotiation skills, effective at all levels up to senior executives.
You can efficiently perform management tasks including incident response and escalations; vendor & contract management; infrastructure management and service resiliency; and service ownership.
You enjoy challenges of working on different types of projects (from large complex to simple).
You collaborate with various business functions to ensure Wealth Technology meets business needs.

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We'd love to work with you if you have:

Individual projects range from Minor Enhancements ($50K+) to major strategic initiatives with $10MM+ budgets in a given year.
Demonstrated success delivering applications in an agile environment, strong organization and planning skills with a track record of successful delivery
Experience in leading and coaching delivery teams, with track record of attracting and developing talent
Critical thinking skills: using logic and reasoning to evaluate alternative solutions, recommendations, summarize conclusions and approaches to mitigate risks
Demonstrated ability to achieve strategic goals
Ability to develop strong working relationships with business and technology partners
Relevant working experience in the financial sector, Wealth and Asset Management experience
Understanding of the regulatory environment and parameters impacting the design and delivery of products and services within the Asset Management industry

What's in it for you?

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Allyship - We strive to create an inclusive culture where every employee is empowered to reach their fullest potential, respected for who they are, and are embraced through bias-free practices and inclusive values across Scotiabank. Scotiabank continues to locate, remove and prevent barriers so that we can build a diverse and inclusive environment while meeting accessibility requirements.

Competitive Rewards program including bonus, flexible vacation, personal, sick days and benefits will start on day one.

jobs.title: Head of Platform Engineering
jobs.description:
Canadian Bank Note Company (CBN) is a leader and trusted provider of secure document and adjacent enterprise-level system solutions across the following domains: border security, civil identity, driver licence/identification and vehicle information, excise control, currency, lotteries and charitable gaming.

Our Corporate Philosophy and 7 Core Principles shape and guide our corporate behaviours and underpin the sense of community you will experience at CBN. We seek long-term relationships with our employees and offer a competitive compensation package that includes health, medical and life insurance benefits and a defined contribution pension plan with company matching.

Job Description

Job Title:
Head of Platform Engineering

Job Type:
Permanent, Full-time

Job Location:
18 Auriga Drive, Ottawa ON

Work Model:
Hybrid

Job Status:
Existing Vacancy

Position Summary

CBN has set out to become the leading global platform provider for managing government ID and ID-enabled services. As Head of Platform Engineering, you will build and run that platform: allowing for applications and services to deploy the same way across environments such as Azure, on-prem Red Hat OpenShift, AWS and air-gapped customer sites, with security and compliance built in by design.

You will lead platform teams, translate CBN's vision into the platform roadmap, own technical direction, and stay close to implementation through design reviews, infrastructure-code reviews and complex production troubleshooting.

Key Responsibilities

Platform Architecture and Scale: Set technical direction, review designs and resolve cross-team technical problems across Azure (AKS, hub-and-spoke landing zones) and Kubernetes/OpenShift. Design for national-scale identity services and hundreds of millions of credential verifications annually.
Engineering and Delivery: Work directly with engineers on GitOps, CI/CD and infrastructure automation using Argo CD, Helm, Terraform and JFrog Artifactory. Establish reusable deployment patterns and go-live standards, including secured registries, offline upgrades and signed release bundles verified at air-gapped sites.
Reliability: Diagnose complex production failures alongside engineers and drive lasting fixes. Set SLOs, observability and capacity requirements using OpenTelemetry and visualization tooling; oversee L2/L3 support and problem management, and verify that backups and disaster recovery work.
Security by Design: Embed security gates, SBOMs, image signing, SAST/DAST and automated SOC 2/ISO 27001 evidence into delivery. Own Platform's control responsibilities with Security (patching, hardening, access reviews, backups/DR), identify and close security deviations at scale and support audits.
AI-Enabled Engineering: Support spec-driven development and enhance agents for delivery, change preparation, incident triage, runbook automation, and human approval with audit trails.
Platform Strategy and Adoption: Translate CBN's vision into a practical roadmap. Work with product, engineering and service delivery teams to onboard jurisdictions, reduce bespoke deployments and improve developer experience. Support platform bids and explain investment, capacity, commitments and risk to executives.
Team and Budget Leadership: Hire and develop strong engineers and team leads, allocate staff across DevOps, Infrastructure and DevEx functions, and hold teams accountable for delivery. Own platform spend and vendor contracts, working with Infrastructure & Operations on cost optimisation.

Qualifications

Mandatory Qualifications

Legally eligible to work in Canada
Fluent in English (speak, read, write)
Able to obtain (in a timely manner) and maintain Government of Canada Secret (Level II) security clearance
Able to work evenings, weekends and holidays as required during security incidents and customer go-lives
Able to travel approx. 1-2 weeks/year

Minimum Qualifications

Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience
Experience: 10+ years in infrastructure or software engineering leadership, including 5+ years managing leads or managers across multiple teams.
Operating Record: Demonstrated improvements in production reliability, performance or operating cost. Able to explain the baseline, engineering changes and resulting outcomes.
Recent Hands-On Engineering: Recent experience writing design specifications, implementing infrastructure or deployment automation, and reviewing code and configurations. Able to diagnose complex production failures alongside engineers.
Technical Depth: Deep practical experience in at least two of the following, with sufficient understanding of distributed systems to assess failure modes and architectural trade-offs:
Kubernetes/OpenShift operations (upgrade strategies, networking, secrets management, cluster reliability)
Azure or AWS infrastructure (well-architected frameworks, FinOps/Cost Management, networking, identity, subscription design strategies)
CI/CD and GitOps (Argo CD, Terraform, Helm, Pipeline Implementation)
Reliability engineering (SLOs/Error Budgets, Monitoring Workspaces, Cross-Region Failover, Chaos Engineering)

Platform Delivery and Adoption: Built or substantially modernised a shared platform from design through production adoption, including upgrades, rollback and operational handover. Experience delivering into regulated, government or disconnected environments, with measurable improvements, e.g. DORA metrics, onboarding time or developer satisfaction.
Secure Automation: Implemented controlled, repeatable releases using infrastructure as code and GitOps.
Technical Leadership: Hired and developed strong engineers and leads, and made technical decisions under competing delivery, reliability, security and cost constraints.
AI in Practice: Used AI agents in delivery or operations with human oversight and an audit trail.
Business Accountability: Owned cloud spend and vendor contracts, and explained platform investment, technical trade-offs and risk to product, finance, Security/GRC and executive stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading or working closely with forward-deployed, solutions or pre-sales engineers, including technical bid and RFP answers
Identity and edge infrastructure: IDP/PAM, PKI, Load Balancing, Zero Trust, CDN/Edge Caching
Policy-as-code and supply-chain security: OPA/Kyverno, SAST/DAST, SBOMs, External Secrets
Microservice and distributed architectures, scalable hub-and-spoke topologies and high-volume data operations

Additional Information

Equal Opportunity Statement

Our organization is committed to employment equity and diversity in the workplace. We actively encourage applications from women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, members of visible minorities, and LGBTQ2+ individuals.

We are dedicated to removing barriers and fostering an inclusive workplace that reflects society and we are committed to providing an accessible and inclusive recruitment process in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA).

If you require accommodation at any stage of the hiring process, please contact us at recruitment@cbnco.com so that appropriate arrangements can be made.

jobs.description:
Location

Brookfield Place - 181 Bay Street

Business - Credit

Brookfield Credit manages approximately $305 billion of assets globally, focused on a broad range of private credit investment strategies, including infrastructure and renewable credit, real estate, asset backed, and corporate credit. Return profiles span investment grade, sub-investment grade, and opportunistic. The business combines Brookfield’s substantial credit history with strategic partners, including Oaktree Capital Management, Castlelake, LCM Partners, 17Capital, and Primary Wave Music. As one of the world’s largest and most experienced credit managers globally, we deliver flexible, specialized capital solutions to borrowers, and attractive risk-adjusted returns to our investors

Brookfield Culture

Brookfield has a unique and dynamic culture. We seek team members who have a long-term focus and whose values align with our Attributes of a Brookfield Leader: Entrepreneurial, Collaborative and Disciplined. Brookfield is committed to the development of our people through challenging work assignments and exposure to diverse businesses.

Job Description

The Director, FP&A will join the Brookfield Credit Group Finance team and will report into Senior Vice President, Finance. The Director will primarily be responsible for supporting Brookfield’s Credit business with planning and forecasting processes, including trend analysis and tracking performance against our financial targets. The successful candidate will prepare clear and thoughtful analyses in support of a large variety of deliverables and presentations. The successful candidate will also work collaboratively with various stakeholders, including the broader finance and operations teams across our partner managers, BAM and BN.

Responsibilities:

Oversee FP&A consolidation for BAM’s global Credit segment, including forecasts, business plans and quarterly non-GAAP results, ensuring completeness, accuracy and appropriate review of key outputs
Own the OneStream FP&A system for the Credit segment, including oversight of system changes, enhancements and ongoing utilization to support management reporting, forecasting and analysis
Serve as first reviewer of consolidated forecasts, actual results and business plans, including detailed analysis of key drivers, trends and variances prior to senior team review
Manage quarterly timelines and deliverables across the Credit Group, ensuring operating company submissions are received, reviewed and submitted to BAM in accordance with required deadlines
Coordinate quarterly earnings, forecast and actuals submissions for Credit Segment into BAM reporting, ensuring submissions are complete, accurate and aligned with required timelines
Perform first review of corporate forecasts prepared by financial analyst, incorporating input from the VP Controller as required
Prepare quarterly Credit sub-segment profitability analysis, including detailed review of performance drivers and trends
Prepare and review quarterly results presentation decks and present results to members of senior management
Serve as a key finance liaison with the Credit segment’s largest subsidiary, supporting its finance team through business planning, reporting and issue resolution
Manage 1–2 Financial Analysts responsible for preparing consolidated forecasts, results and business plans, while remaining hands-on in detailed review, analysis and execution of core FP&A deliverables
Build strong relationships across the organization and with portfolio companies, fostering open communication, collaboration and effective problem-solving to support timely, accurate and decision-useful reporting
Identify and implement process improvements to increase efficiency, productivity and scalability of FP&A reporting, forecasting and analysis

Qualifications & Requirements:

Degree in finance, accounting or related business discipline and CPA designation
8+ years of progressive experience in FP&A or Financial Reporting
1-2 years of professional finance management experience
Expert with MS Office (MS Excel, PowerPoint); Experience with OneStream a plus
Strong quantitative and analytical skills, sound judgment, and the ability to assess complex situations and make clear recommendations
Highly organized self-starter with strong communication skills, sound professional ethics, and a commitment to continuous improvement

Salary Range: $150,000 - $170,000 CAD

jobs.description:
About The Team

The Technical Support team is responsible for ensuring that developers and enterprises can reliably build mission critical solutions using OpenAI models. We provide technical guidance, resolve complex issues and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our highly-capable models. We work closely with Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. We think from an automation-first mindset and leverage the latest in AI to scale our support operations. Join the Senior Support Engineering (SSE) team at OpenAI and help shape the future of Technical Support in the age of AI.

About The Role

We are looking for a Senior Support Engineer to collaborate directly with our strategic enterprise accounts and product teams, helping solve some of the most difficult problems faced by our Customers. You will be part of the best technical troubleshooting team at OpenAI, and our Customers and Engineering teams will look to you for technical guidance in addressing the most technically difficult issues in our environment.

As a Senior Support Engineer, you will design and run operational processes to monitor our top strategic customers and a 24x7 response team. You’ll work closely with our Infrastructure and Engineering teams to deliver the best possible experience to customers at scale. Working directly with our most strategic Customers - You will be crucial to the success of the most innovative, disruptive, and high-scale AI solutions being built with the OpenAI API platform.

The nature of this role will be low volume, high difficulty.

This Toronto-based role is currently remote and is expected to transition to an in-office arrangement.

In This Role, You Will

Be among the foremost technical and troubleshooting experts for our API platform at OpenAI. You are the last line of defense before the core Engineering team.
Proactively identify and implement opportunities to scale support operations by leveraging automation and advancements in AI technologies. Contribute to shaping the future of technical support in an AI-driven era.
Configure and use advanced monitoring and alerting workflows to proactively detect customer impacting issues in real time.
In partnership with engineering, contribute to reliability reviews and preparedness for new features, launches, or strategic customer requirement updates. Ensure that operational readiness (monitoring, alerting, and fallback plans) is in place for any such changes.
Design and refine incident response processes and documentation across strategic customers, engineering and support teams.
Analyze operational metrics and incident RCAs to identify areas for improvement. Proactively recommend and implement enhancements to monitoring dashboards, alert configurations, and support workflows.
Provide support coverage during holidays and weekends based on business needs.

You Might Thrive In This Role If You

Have a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field. A strong software engineering foundation is important for this role’s success.
Have 8+ years of experience in technical operations roles such as SRE/NOC, designing monitoring systems and resolving production issues in fast-paced and mission-critical environments. A strong track record of troubleshooting complex technical problems at the systems level.
Have deep familiarity with modern monitoring, alerting, and observability practices. Hands‑on experience setting up or managing metrics, logging, and tracing for distributed systems (e.g., understanding of SLIs/SLOs, alert tuning, dashboard creation).
Have proven experience leading incident response for high‑severity outages or service disruptions. Able to perform real‑time incident coordination, root cause analysis, and drive follow‑ups (post‑mortems, action items) to prevent recurrence. Knowledge of industry best practices for incident management and fault diagnosis.
Have strong skills in scripting or software engineering (e.g., Python or similar) to automate repetitive tasks and integrate tools.
Have solid understanding of cloud infrastructure and distributed systems fundamentals. Comfortable working with cloud services, load balancers, databases, and containerized applications.
Are effective at working cross‑functionally in a high‑trust environment. Strong communication skills to explain technical issues and resolutions to both engineering and non‑technical stakeholders. You can coordinate efforts across teams and are comfortable providing updates in the midst of an ongoing incident.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

jobs.title: Director of Financial Planning and Analysis
jobs.description:
ABOUT TRINDENT

Trindent Consulting is a global management consulting firm that specializes in technical augmentation in the energy sector, specifically downstream oil & gas and large energy users. We are a profit improvement firm, first and foremost. Trindent Consulting specializes in process engineering & optimization.
Without capital investment we create actionable ways to sustainably increase refinery margins by 2–3%. We’ve helped over 100 clients achieve significant financial benefits that yield between 500–1500% return-on-investment within the 1st year – and we’ve done that without capital investments or software changes of any kind.
Established in 2008, Trindent Consulting has quickly garnered a reputation as a firm that Makes It Happen™. We are ranked as one of Canada’s Fastest-Growing Companies by Canadian Business and GROWTH 500 for 7 years in a row. In September 2026 our 290% 3-Year Revenue Growth was rewarded with being named in Globe & Mail’s 2026 Fastest growing companies in Canada. Trindent Consulting is the 5th fastest growing Professional & Technical Services company in Canada.

Refineries are extraordinarily complex businesses. Trindent specializes in several ultra-high value niches within refineries where tens of millions of dollars in performance improvement may be captured in the short-term. Underpinned by data analytics, industry know-how, and technical experience; Trindent has implemented improvement engagements in over 40 refineries globally.

BUSINESS EXPANSION

Our practice is expanding. As part of this growth, we are building a strong pipeline of experienced professionals to support client engagements. We are gearing up for 20–25% growth and we hope you will join us on this journey!

THE OPPORTUNITY

Trindent Consulting is seeking a Director of Financial Planning & Analysis
to lead the evolution of Finance from a predominantly transactional accounting function into a commercially focused management finance organization.
This is a senior, hands-on leadership role responsible for building the planning, reporting, analytics and decision-support capabilities required to support Trindent’s continued growth. The Director will provide leadership with reliable financial information, actionable commercial insight and clear recommendations that strengthen operational control, improve project profitability, deliver measurable cost savings and enable better delegation of authority.
The successful candidate will establish an integrated view of Trindent’s financial and operational performance, connecting project revenue, consultant labour, utilization, expenses, margin realization, headcount, cash flow and investment decisions. They will work closely with the President, Finance Director, Executive and Leadership Teams, project leaders and functional budget owners to translate company strategy into financial targets, operating plans and accountable actions.

This role requires someone who can operate strategically while remaining close to the detail: building models, challenging assumptions, improving data quality, resolving reporting gaps and explaining financial performance clearly to senior leadership and the Board.

The Director of FP&A will be charged with establishing five foundational management finance capabilities.

1. Project-Based Financial Reporting

Design and implement a standardized Sold vs. Plan vs. Actual
reporting framework for all major assessments and engagements.
Provide clear project-level visibility into:
Contracted and recognized revenue.
Planned and actual consultant labour.
Consultant utilization and resource deployment.
Travel and other project expenses.
Gross margin and margin realization.
Forecast-to-complete and expected final project outcome.
Material financial and operational variance drivers.
Establish consistent project definitions, financial assumptions, data sources, ownership and reporting timelines.
Introduce recurring project financial reviews that identify emerging margin risks, delivery issues, corrective actions and accountable owners.
Ensure project reporting supports stronger engagement governance, resource planning, commercial decision-making and margin management.

2. Executive Management Reporting

Implement a reliable monthly management reporting package for the President, Finance Director, Executive and Leadership Teams.
Provide concise analysis of:
Revenue and project profitability.
Gross margin and operating performance.
Cash flow and working capital.
Budget and forecast variances.
Consultant utilization, headcount and labour cost.
Travel and operational expenditure.
Cost-saving performance.
Key risks, opportunities and required decisions.
Move reporting beyond retrospective results by explaining what happened, why it happened, what is expected next and what action is recommended
.
Clearly distinguish final, provisional, estimated and unavailable information, with named owners and deadlines for resolving material data issues.
Establish a recurring reporting calendar, review cadence and approval process that leadership can rely on.

3. Cost Savings and Expense Optimization

Launch a structured cost-optimization program covering travel, procurement, vendor management and operational spending.
Prioritize opportunities relating to:
Airline and hotel expenditure.
Foreign-exchange and payment fees.
Cancellation and change charges.
Vendor pricing and service levels.
Contract compliance.
Duplicate, avoidable or uncontrolled expenditure.
Quantify business cases, establish financial baselines and maintain a formal savings register.
Distinguish identified, approved, implemented and realized savings to ensure benefits are measurable and verifiable.
Turn cost analysis into practical recommendations on what to renegotiate, consolidate, defer, reduce or stop—without undermining client delivery or sustainable growth.

4. Governance and Financial Controls

Strengthen financial governance through clearer approval authorities, spending controls, vendor oversight, payment controls and project performance reviews.
Introduce vendor scorecards covering cost, service, responsiveness, contract compliance and performance.
Establish recurring financial and operating reviews with clear agendas, decision rights, actions, owners and completion dates.
Improve controls over budget commitments, purchase decisions, project expenditure and forecast changes.
Work closely with Accounting to define a disciplined month-end handover covering required inputs, reconciliation checks, delivery dates, data ownership and escalation routes.
Improve transparency and control while avoiding unnecessary bureaucracy or slowing operational decision-making.

5. Board and Leadership Readiness

Develop Board-ready financial reporting covering:
Overall financial performance.
Project and portfolio profitability.
Revenue, margin and cash-flow trends.
Operational and professional-services KPIs.
Material risks and opportunities.
Cost-optimization performance.
Progress against the Finance transformation roadmap.
Ensure Board and leadership materials are concise, accurate, reconciled and supported by clear analysis.
Maintain models, assumptions and supporting evidence in a due-diligence-ready state.
Provide the President, Finance Director and senior leadership with scenario analysis, recommendations and decision papers that enable confident and timely action.

QUALIFICATIONS

A recognized accounting or finance qualification such as CPA, CA, ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CFA or an equivalent professional designation.

KEY SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

10 years+ business and operational finance track record working for a fast growth services business operating across multiple legal entities, currencies & countries.
Experience in a consulting, professional-services, project-based or people-intensive business connecting project revenue, labour deployment, utilization, expenses, headcount and cash flow.
Experience building
or materially upgrading an FP&A function.
Advanced financial modelling, forecasting, scenario analysis and sensitivity analysis.
Strong project-profitability, margin-analysis variance, trend and root-cause analysis capability.
Strong data reconciliation, model-control and documentation discipline.
Advanced spreadsheet capability and experience working with ERP, planning, reporting or business-intelligence platforms.
Ability to design executive dashboards and communicate financial and operational KPIs clearly.
Strong business-case development, investment evaluation and decision-support capability.
Ability to translate complex financial information into concise, commercially relevant recommendations.

WORK LOCATION & FLEXIBILITY

This position may be based in either Dublin, Ireland or Toronto, Canada.

Trindent Consulting is looking for a FP&A Director who can modernize our financial reporting, provide deep insights and help us Make it Happen
as we grow our global revenues and customer base.

new_jobs.title: Head of Platform Engineering
new_jobs.description:
Canadian Bank Note Company (CBN) is a leader and trusted provider of secure document and adjacent enterprise-level system solutions across the following domains: border security, civil identity, driver licence/identification and vehicle information, excise control, currency, lotteries and charitable gaming.

Our Corporate Philosophy and 7 Core Principles shape and guide our corporate behaviours and underpin the sense of community you will experience at CBN. We seek long-term relationships with our employees and offer a competitive compensation package that includes health, medical and life insurance benefits and a defined contribution pension plan with company matching.

Job Description

Job Title:
Head of Platform Engineering

Job Type:
Permanent, Full-time

Job Location:
18 Auriga Drive, Ottawa ON

Work Model:
Hybrid

Job Status:
Existing Vacancy

Position Summary

CBN has set out to become the leading global platform provider for managing government ID and ID-enabled services. As Head of Platform Engineering, you will build and run that platform: allowing for applications and services to deploy the same way across environments such as Azure, on-prem Red Hat OpenShift, AWS and air-gapped customer sites, with security and compliance built in by design.

You will lead platform teams, translate CBN's vision into the platform roadmap, own technical direction, and stay close to implementation through design reviews, infrastructure-code reviews and complex production troubleshooting.

Key Responsibilities

Platform Architecture and Scale: Set technical direction, review designs and resolve cross-team technical problems across Azure (AKS, hub-and-spoke landing zones) and Kubernetes/OpenShift. Design for national-scale identity services and hundreds of millions of credential verifications annually.
Engineering and Delivery: Work directly with engineers on GitOps, CI/CD and infrastructure automation using Argo CD, Helm, Terraform and JFrog Artifactory. Establish reusable deployment patterns and go-live standards, including secured registries, offline upgrades and signed release bundles verified at air-gapped sites.
Reliability: Diagnose complex production failures alongside engineers and drive lasting fixes. Set SLOs, observability and capacity requirements using OpenTelemetry and visualization tooling; oversee L2/L3 support and problem management, and verify that backups and disaster recovery work.
Security by Design: Embed security gates, SBOMs, image signing, SAST/DAST and automated SOC 2/ISO 27001 evidence into delivery. Own Platform's control responsibilities with Security (patching, hardening, access reviews, backups/DR), identify and close security deviations at scale and support audits.
AI-Enabled Engineering: Support spec-driven development and enhance agents for delivery, change preparation, incident triage, runbook automation, and human approval with audit trails.
Platform Strategy and Adoption: Translate CBN's vision into a practical roadmap. Work with product, engineering and service delivery teams to onboard jurisdictions, reduce bespoke deployments and improve developer experience. Support platform bids and explain investment, capacity, commitments and risk to executives.
Team and Budget Leadership: Hire and develop strong engineers and team leads, allocate staff across DevOps, Infrastructure and DevEx functions, and hold teams accountable for delivery. Own platform spend and vendor contracts, working with Infrastructure & Operations on cost optimisation.

Qualifications

Mandatory Qualifications

Legally eligible to work in Canada
Fluent in English (speak, read, write)
Able to obtain (in a timely manner) and maintain Government of Canada Secret (Level II) security clearance
Able to work evenings, weekends and holidays as required during security incidents and customer go-lives
Able to travel approx. 1-2 weeks/year

Minimum Qualifications

Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience
Experience: 10+ years in infrastructure or software engineering leadership, including 5+ years managing leads or managers across multiple teams.
Operating Record: Demonstrated improvements in production reliability, performance or operating cost. Able to explain the baseline, engineering changes and resulting outcomes.
Recent Hands-On Engineering: Recent experience writing design specifications, implementing infrastructure or deployment automation, and reviewing code and configurations. Able to diagnose complex production failures alongside engineers.
Technical Depth: Deep practical experience in at least two of the following, with sufficient understanding of distributed systems to assess failure modes and architectural trade-offs:
Kubernetes/OpenShift operations (upgrade strategies, networking, secrets management, cluster reliability)
Azure or AWS infrastructure (well-architected frameworks, FinOps/Cost Management, networking, identity, subscription design strategies)
CI/CD and GitOps (Argo CD, Terraform, Helm, Pipeline Implementation)
Reliability engineering (SLOs/Error Budgets, Monitoring Workspaces, Cross-Region Failover, Chaos Engineering)

Platform Delivery and Adoption: Built or substantially modernised a shared platform from design through production adoption, including upgrades, rollback and operational handover. Experience delivering into regulated, government or disconnected environments, with measurable improvements, e.g. DORA metrics, onboarding time or developer satisfaction.
Secure Automation: Implemented controlled, repeatable releases using infrastructure as code and GitOps.
Technical Leadership: Hired and developed strong engineers and leads, and made technical decisions under competing delivery, reliability, security and cost constraints.
AI in Practice: Used AI agents in delivery or operations with human oversight and an audit trail.
Business Accountability: Owned cloud spend and vendor contracts, and explained platform investment, technical trade-offs and risk to product, finance, Security/GRC and executive stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading or working closely with forward-deployed, solutions or pre-sales engineers, including technical bid and RFP answers
Identity and edge infrastructure: IDP/PAM, PKI, Load Balancing, Zero Trust, CDN/Edge Caching
Policy-as-code and supply-chain security: OPA/Kyverno, SAST/DAST, SBOMs, External Secrets
Microservice and distributed architectures, scalable hub-and-spoke topologies and high-volume data operations

Brookfield Credit manages approximately $305 billion of assets globally, focused on a broad range of private credit investment strategies, including infrastructure and renewable credit, real estate, asset backed, and corporate credit. Brookfield is committed to the development of our people through challenging work assignments and exposure to diverse businesses.

Job Description

The Director, FP&A will join the Brookfield Credit Group Finance team and will report into Senior Vice President, Finance. The Director will primarily be responsible for supporting Brookfield’s Credit business with planning and forecasting processes, including trend analysis and tracking performance against our financial targets. The successful candidate will prepare clear and thoughtful analyses in support of a large variety of deliverables and presentations. The successful candidate will also work collaboratively with various stakeholders, including the broader finance and operations teams across our partner managers, BAM and BN.

Responsibilities:

Oversee FP&A consolidation for BAM’s global Credit segment, including forecasts, business plans and quarterly non-GAAP results, ensuring completeness, accuracy and appropriate review of key outputs
Own the OneStream FP&A system for the Credit segment, including oversight of system changes, enhancements and ongoing utilization to support management reporting, forecasting and analysis
Serve as first reviewer of consolidated forecasts, actual results and business plans, including detailed analysis of key drivers, trends and variances prior to senior team review
Manage quarterly timelines and deliverables across the Credit Group, ensuring operating company submissions are received, reviewed and submitted to BAM in accordance with required deadlines
Coordinate quarterly earnings, forecast and actuals submissions for Credit Segment into BAM reporting, ensuring submissions are complete, accurate and aligned with required timelines
Perform first review of corporate forecasts prepared by financial analyst, incorporating input from the VP Controller as required
Prepare quarterly Credit sub-segment profitability analysis, including detailed review of performance drivers and trends
Prepare and review quarterly results presentation decks and present results to members of senior management
Serve as a key finance liaison with the Credit segment’s largest subsidiary, supporting its finance team through business planning, reporting and issue resolution
Manage 1–2 Financial Analysts responsible for preparing consolidated forecasts, results and business plans, while remaining hands-on in detailed review, analysis and execution of core FP&A deliverables
Build strong relationships across the organization and with portfolio companies, fostering open communication, collaboration and effective problem-solving to support timely, accurate and decision-useful reporting
Identify and implement process improvements to increase efficiency, productivity and scalability of FP&A reporting, forecasting and analysis

Degree in finance, accounting or related business discipline and CPA designation
8+ years of progressive experience in FP&A or Financial Reporting

Strong quantitative and analytical skills, sound judgment, and the ability to assess complex situations and make clear recommendations

new_jobs.title: Director of Financial Planning and Analysis
new_jobs.description:
ABOUT TRINDENT

Trindent Consulting is a global management consulting firm that specializes in technical augmentation in the energy sector, specifically downstream oil & gas and large energy users. We are a profit improvement firm, first and foremost. Trindent Consulting specializes in process engineering & optimization.
Without capital investment we create actionable ways to sustainably increase refinery margins by 2–3%. We’ve helped over 100 clients achieve significant financial benefits that yield between 500–1500% return-on-investment within the 1st year – and we’ve done that without capital investments or software changes of any kind.
Established in 2008, Trindent Consulting has quickly garnered a reputation as a firm that Makes It Happen™. We are ranked as one of Canada’s Fastest-Growing Companies by Canadian Business and GROWTH 500 for 7 years in a row. In September 2026 our 290% 3-Year Revenue Growth was rewarded with being named in Globe & Mail’s 2026 Fastest growing companies in Canada. Trindent Consulting is the 5th fastest growing Professional & Technical Services company in Canada.

Refineries are extraordinarily complex businesses. Trindent specializes in several ultra-high value niches within refineries where tens of millions of dollars in performance improvement may be captured in the short-term. Underpinned by data analytics, industry know-how, and technical experience; Trindent has implemented improvement engagements in over 40 refineries globally.

BUSINESS EXPANSION

Our practice is expanding. As part of this growth, we are building a strong pipeline of experienced professionals to support client engagements. We are gearing up for 20–25% growth and we hope you will join us on this journey!

THE OPPORTUNITY

Trindent Consulting is seeking a Director of Financial Planning & Analysis
to lead the evolution of Finance from a predominantly transactional accounting function into a commercially focused management finance organization.
This is a senior, hands-on leadership role responsible for building the planning, reporting, analytics and decision-support capabilities required to support Trindent’s continued growth. The Director will provide leadership with reliable financial information, actionable commercial insight and clear recommendations that strengthen operational control, improve project profitability, deliver measurable cost savings and enable better delegation of authority.
The successful candidate will establish an integrated view of Trindent’s financial and operational performance, connecting project revenue, consultant labour, utilization, expenses, margin realization, headcount, cash flow and investment decisions. They will work closely with the President, Finance Director, Executive and Leadership Teams, project leaders and functional budget owners to translate company strategy into financial targets, operating plans and accountable actions.

This role requires someone who can operate strategically while remaining close to the detail: building models, challenging assumptions, improving data quality, resolving reporting gaps and explaining financial performance clearly to senior leadership and the Board.

The Director of FP&A will be charged with establishing five foundational management finance capabilities.

1. Project-Based Financial Reporting

Design and implement a standardized Sold vs. Plan vs. Actual
reporting framework for all major assessments and engagements.
Provide clear project-level visibility into:
Contracted and recognized revenue.
Planned and actual consultant labour.
Consultant utilization and resource deployment.
Travel and other project expenses.
Gross margin and margin realization.
Forecast-to-complete and expected final project outcome.
Material financial and operational variance drivers.
Establish consistent project definitions, financial assumptions, data sources, ownership and reporting timelines.
Introduce recurring project financial reviews that identify emerging margin risks, delivery issues, corrective actions and accountable owners.
Ensure project reporting supports stronger engagement governance, resource planning, commercial decision-making and margin management.

2. Executive Management Reporting

Implement a reliable monthly management reporting package for the President, Finance Director, Executive and Leadership Teams.
Provide concise analysis of:
Revenue and project profitability.
Gross margin and operating performance.
Cash flow and working capital.
Budget and forecast variances.
Consultant utilization, headcount and labour cost.
Travel and operational expenditure.
Cost-saving performance.
Key risks, opportunities and required decisions.
Move reporting beyond retrospective results by explaining what happened, why it happened, what is expected next and what action is recommended
.
Clearly distinguish final, provisional, estimated and unavailable information, with named owners and deadlines for resolving material data issues.
Establish a recurring reporting calendar, review cadence and approval process that leadership can rely on.

3. Cost Savings and Expense Optimization

Launch a structured cost-optimization program covering travel, procurement, vendor management and operational spending.
Prioritize opportunities relating to:
Airline and hotel expenditure.
Foreign-exchange and payment fees.
Cancellation and change charges.
Vendor pricing and service levels.
Contract compliance.
Duplicate, avoidable or uncontrolled expenditure.
Quantify business cases, establish financial baselines and maintain a formal savings register.
Distinguish identified, approved, implemented and realized savings to ensure benefits are measurable and verifiable.
Turn cost analysis into practical recommendations on what to renegotiate, consolidate, defer, reduce or stop—without undermining client delivery or sustainable growth.

4. Governance and Financial Controls

Strengthen financial governance through clearer approval authorities, spending controls, vendor oversight, payment controls and project performance reviews.
Introduce vendor scorecards covering cost, service, responsiveness, contract compliance and performance.
Establish recurring financial and operating reviews with clear agendas, decision rights, actions, owners and completion dates.
Improve controls over budget commitments, purchase decisions, project expenditure and forecast changes.
Work closely with Accounting to define a disciplined month-end handover covering required inputs, reconciliation checks, delivery dates, data ownership and escalation routes.
Improve transparency and control while avoiding unnecessary bureaucracy or slowing operational decision-making.

5. Board and Leadership Readiness

Develop Board-ready financial reporting covering:
Overall financial performance.
Project and portfolio profitability.
Revenue, margin and cash-flow trends.
Operational and professional-services KPIs.
Material risks and opportunities.
Cost-optimization performance.
Progress against the Finance transformation roadmap.
Ensure Board and leadership materials are concise, accurate, reconciled and supported by clear analysis.
Maintain models, assumptions and supporting evidence in a due-diligence-ready state.
Provide the President, Finance Director and senior leadership with scenario analysis, recommendations and decision papers that enable confident and timely action.

QUALIFICATIONS

A recognized accounting or finance qualification such as CPA, CA, ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CFA or an equivalent professional designation.

KEY SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

10 years+ business and operational finance track record working for a fast growth services business operating across multiple legal entities, currencies & countries.
Experience in a consulting, professional-services, project-based or people-intensive business connecting project revenue, labour deployment, utilization, expenses, headcount and cash flow.
Experience building
or materially upgrading an FP&A function.
Advanced financial modelling, forecasting, scenario analysis and sensitivity analysis.
Strong project-profitability, margin-analysis variance, trend and root-cause analysis capability.
Strong data reconciliation, model-control and documentation discipline.
Advanced spreadsheet capability and experience working with ERP, planning, reporting or business-intelligence platforms.
Ability to design executive dashboards and communicate financial and operational KPIs clearly.
Strong business-case development, investment evaluation and decision-support capability.
Ability to translate complex financial information into concise, commercially relevant recommendations.

WORK LOCATION & FLEXIBILITY

This position may be based in either Dublin, Ireland or Toronto, Canada.

Trindent Consulting is looking for a FP&A Director who can modernize our financial reporting, provide deep insights and help us Make it Happen
as we grow our global revenues and customer base.
